stories.headline: Democrats Sweep Congress as GOP Blames the Iran War
stories.dek: Democrats flipped the House and Senate, and Republicans are arguing over whether the war, Trump or the economy sank them.
pole_a_bullets: The losses trace to war-driven gas prices, a specific and fixable cost, not a rejection of conservative policy.
Midterms punish the president's party, and Trump wasn't on the ballot. His handpicked candidates carried that burden.
Divided government limits new spending and taxes. Markets liked the gridlock, with the Dow up about 1,500 points Wednesday.
The president still commands the military. Democratic probes risk turning national security into partisan theater.
pole_b_bullets: Voters rejected a costly war, corruption and high prices, and Democrats won even in deep-red Texas, Kansas and South Carolina.
Congress controls the purse. Schumer says the war must end, and Jeffries wants Trump to stop before January.
Oversight is overdue. Senate Democrats have already sent document-preservation letters ahead of investigations.
The mandate is affordability. Tariffs and war-driven oil prices raised costs, and Jeffries says easing them comes first.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by Republican strategists, GOP leaders and conservative commentators.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by Democratic leaders, progressive lawmakers and liberal commentators.
evidence_left: Democrats hold 54 Senate seats to the GOP's 44, with Alaska and Mississippi still unresolved, per CBS and Yahoo News.
CBS projects House Democrats will hold 251 to 268 seats.
evidence_right: Vance said the war was why Republicans lost. Trump also called it part of the reason but defended launching it.
Speaker Mike Johnson won't seek re-election as House GOP leader, TIME reported.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CBS News, CNN, TIME, MS NOW, Yahoo News and CNBC, November 5, 2026.

stories.headline: AI Chip Stocks Crater on Fears of Data-Center Curbs
stories.dek: The Nasdaq-100 fell 6.4% as investors bet Democratic officials will slow the AI buildout.
pole_a_bullets: Demand hasn't gone away. AMD's Lisa Su says demand outstrips supply and expects revenue growth above 80% in 2027.
Blanket moratoria would hit hardest in Texas, which holds a large share of planned US data-center capacity.
A patchwork of state rules and pauses slows the US in its race with China. Federal policy has aimed at a single standard.
The selloff looks overdone. Nvidia's forward P/E is at a five-year low while analysts see its earnings more than doubling.
pole_b_bullets: Voters asked for limits. Most of the 41 ballot measures on slowing data centers passed.
Power-hungry data centers raise electricity bills. Developers should pay their own grid costs.
Ohio's Gov.-elect Acton backs a conditional pause unless builders cover 100% of utility costs, a middle path rather than a ban.
Early safety rules and scaled-back tax breaks are overdue. Some analysts say pushback could deflate a bubble without popping it.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by chipmakers, AI-industry executives and pro-buildout analysts.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by Democratic governors-elect, consumer advocates and AI-safety and utility-cost critics.
evidence_left: The Nasdaq-100 fell 6.4%, wiping out $2.3 trillion in its worst session since March 2020, per Bloomberg.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell more than 12%, and Nvidia fell about 9%, per Fox Business.
evidence_right: Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa pledged an immediate data-center moratorium. Ohio's Amy Acton backs a conditional one.
UBS estimates roughly 30% of expected 2028 US data-center capacity additions could face construction pauses.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from Bloomberg, Fortune, Forbes, Fox Business, Yahoo Finance and The National, November 5, 2026.

stories.headline: Wall Street's Post-Election Rally Reverses in an AI Rout
stories.dek: The S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq entered a correction, a day after the Dow's best session since April 2025.
pole_a_bullets: The Wednesday rally showed investors welcome divided government, and the Dow gained about 3%.
This looks like a sector reset tied to data-center politics, not a broken economy. Earnings from AMD and others remain strong.
Oil fell after the midterms on hopes of a deal to end the Iran war, which would ease inflation pressure.
The S&P 500 is still up for 2026, and fear-driven selloffs like this often create buying opportunities.
pole_b_bullets: The selloff was broad. All 11 S&P 500 sectors fell, and the VIX hit its highest level since March.
Inflation is reaccelerating. Cleveland Fed nowcasts point to PCE near 3.8% in October, keeping a December hike in play.
The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% with two dissents for a hike, so relief from rates is not coming soon.
AI spending drove market gains. If data-center growth slows, a heavy part of the market loses its engine.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by equity strategists and dip-buying market commentators.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by inflation-focused economists and valuation skeptics.
evidence_left: The Dow fell 1,833 points, or 3.44%, to 51,523. The S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315, per CNBC.
On Wednesday the Dow jumped more than 1,500 points, its best day since April 2025.
evidence_right: The Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% on Oct. 28, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike.
The economy added just 29,000 jobs in September, and the October jobs report is due Friday, per Schwab.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CNBC, Yahoo Finance, Bloomberg, Schwab and The Motley Fool, November 5, 2026.

stories.headline: Novo Raises Outlook Again as Wegovy Pill Beats Forecasts
stories.dek: The obesity drugmaker lifted 2026 guidance for the third time even as US injectable sales slid.
pole_a_bullets: Pill sales of DKK 5.39 billion beat forecasts and grew 53% from the prior quarter.
Novo estimates it holds about 80% of new US pill prescriptions, so it is winning the funnel for future refills.
Rollout to more than 20 markets next year widens the addressable base.
Adjusted operating profit rose 27%, which shows the turnaround is reaching profits.
pole_b_bullets: Management still expects US sales to fall in 2026, so this is a smaller decline, not growth.
US injectable Wegovy fell 13%, and the pill is still a small share of expected Wegovy sales.
Eli Lilly remains a strong competitor, and patent expiries loom.
The stock has lost about two-thirds of its value since June 2024, and one good quarter doesn't rebuild that.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by pharma bulls and growth investors.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by cautious analysts and risk-focused investors.
evidence_left: Wegovy pill sales were DKK 5.39 billion (about $810 million) against about DKK 4.62 billion expected.
Guidance is now -2% to +2% at constant exchange rates, raised from an earlier range allowing declines of up to 6%.
evidence_right: US injectable Wegovy sales fell 13%, though combined US Wegovy sales rose 21%.
Novo still expects US sales to decline in 2026 and lists slowing pill prescriptions and Lilly competition as risks.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from Reuters (via Euronext), BioPharma Dive, Finimize and Value the Markets, November 4-5, 2026.

stories.headline: MLB Pitches Delayed Salary Cap; Players Say No
stories.dek: Owners moved the cap to 2028 and raised its figure, but the union rejected it with a Dec. 1 lockout looming.
pole_a_bullets: Revenue gaps between clubs are huge, and a cap and floor is the clearest fix for competitive balance.
The NBA, NFL and NHL all run on caps, and their players still thrive.
The floor would force 12 clubs to add about $636 million in payroll, money that would reach players.
Delaying the cap to 2028 and raising it to $258.2 million shows real flexibility.
pole_b_bullets: A cap that caps player pay is a non-starter. The union has opposed one for decades.
Owners last proposed a cap in 1994, and that fight ended in a strike that cancelled the World Series.
The cap includes benefits, and teams wouldn't have to hit the floor every season, so the floor is weaker than advertised.
Players want expanded free agency, a nearly doubled minimum and more revenue sharing. Offering earlier free agency only if they take a cap is a bargaining chip.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by owners, Commissioner Manfred and cap-friendly analysts.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by the MLBPA, players and labor-side commentators.
evidence_left: MLB's new cap is $258.2 million and its floor $180.2 million, up from $245.3 million and $171.2 million.
The league would grant free agency at five service years, down from six, for players 30 and older, but only if the union accepts the cap.
evidence_right: The labor deal expires Dec. 1, and a lockout appears imminent, per ESPN.
The union quickly rejected the proposal, and baseball players have said they will never agree to a cap.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from ESPN, Sports Illustrated, NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports and Forbes, November 3-5, 2026.

stories.headline: Wembanyama Drops 52 as Spurs Edge Mavericks, 112-111
stories.dek: His career night sparked MVP chants, but betting markets still have Luka Doncic as the favorite.
pole_a_bullets: Wemby is the MVP. No one else scores 52 and grabs 24 rebounds with eight blocks in one game.
He is the first player in 30 seasons with 25 points, 10 rebounds and five blocks in a half.
He scored 10 of the Spurs' last 12 points and hit the winning free throw. Stars are supposed to close like that.
San Antonio has won six straight with him as the center of everything.
pole_b_bullets: One game is not a season. Kalshi still lists Luka Doncic as MVP frontrunner after a hot start.
The Spurs blew a 19-point lead and won by one. A missed Kyrie Irving shot saved them.
Wemby shot 1 of 8 from three. Efficiency and durability decide MVP races.
It's early November. MVP voters reward team records over an 82-game season, not a single box score.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by Spurs fans and Wembanyama-MVP advocates.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by Doncic backers and skeptics of early-season MVP talk.
evidence_left: Wembanyama had 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks in the 112-111 win, per Al Jazeera and SI.
His winning free throw came with 24.2 seconds left, and it was the Spurs' sixth straight win.
evidence_right: Kalshi lists Luka Doncic as the NBA MVP frontrunner after a hot start, per Sports Illustrated.
San Antonio had to rally after giving up a 19-point lead, and Wembanyama made one of eight three-pointers.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from Al Jazeera, Sports Illustrated, Yahoo Sports/ClutchPoints and ESPN, November 5, 2026.
